meta.units: meters (NGSIM feet x 0.3048); sigma in meters; probabilities in [0,1]

axes.x: lateral (NGSIM Local_X; + = to the right, toward higher lane IDs)
axes.origin: ego vehicle position at prediction time t (last history point is (0,0))

history.note: frames t-30..t at 10 Hz, every 2nd frame; includes t

meta.model_coordinates_note: The BATraj loader feeds the model POLAR coordinates (r in ft, phi in rad, ego-centric) and the decoder outputs a bivariate Gaussian (mu_r, mu_phi, sigma_r, sigma_phi, rho) in that polar space. Predictions here were converted to Cartesian; sigma_x/sigma_y/rho_xy are first-order (Jacobian) transforms of the polar Gaussian. The project evaluate_model() computes RMSE as sqrt(dr^2 + dphi^2)*0.3048, mixing ft and rad, so the previously reported "RMSE" (6.97 / 7.28 m) is essentially a radial-distance error and ignores most lateral error. Both the reported metric and true Cartesian metrics are included.
meta.mode_selection: prediction = mode of argmax lateral x argmax longitudinal maneuver probability (same as evaluate_model)

attack.model: PrivacyAttackMLP (attack_generic.py): 64->128->128->64->32->2, BatchNorm+ReLU+Dropout, Adam lr 2e-4 wd 1e-4, 50 epochs, batch 512, best-val-loss weights
attack.train_data: 20% random subset of NGSIM TrainSet.mat split 70/10/20 (np seed 72 from battraj.config); attacker never saw TestSet.mat
attack.private_attribute: recording location: dsId 1-3 = US-101 (0), dsId 4-6 = I-80 (1)
attack.retrain_note: Same PrivacyAttackMLP + train_attack_model recipe (Adam 2e-4, wd 1e-4, 50 epochs, batch 512, class-weighted CE, ReduceLROnPlateau, best-val-loss weights), torch seed 72, same 70/10/20 split of 20% of TrainSet (np seed 72), but on batch-1 representations. These attackers produce all headline accuracies, grid and per-scene probabilities. The saved batch-512 attackers are reported only as reference.

meta.maneuver_labels: dataset lateral maneuver label D[:,6] (preprocess_data.m): lane ID change within +-4 s of t; 1 keep, 2 left, 3 right. Lane-change scenes were additionally required to show >=2.5 m lateral displacement in the correct direction over the 5 s future so the change is visible; keep-lane scenes |dx|<1 m.
meta.scene_selection: 12 per maneuver (6 US-101 + 6 I-80), only full 5 s futures; rng seed 12. challenging=true: lane changes with max(FDE_A, FDE_B) >= 95th percentile of the visible-lane-change pool (1 per maneuver x location = 4); other lane-change scenes drawn below the 80th percentile.
meta.grid_selection: 100 TestSet indices, np.random.default_rng(2026).choice(N, 100, replace=False); same samples for A and B
meta.input_features_note: TestSet.mat tracks hold only (frame, Local_X, Local_Y), so the velocity/acceleration, lane and vehicle-class inputs of GDEncoder (f_length=12) are all zeros in this pipeline; the model effectively sees positions only.
meta.neighbors_note: surrounding vehicles = the 13x3 occupancy grid used by the model (grid_lane_col 0/1/2 = left/same/right lane, grid_row 0..12 longitudinal); pos_t = position at t; history/future in the same ego frame (future_gt is ground truth, not a model input).
meta.batch_size_note: EVERYTHING in this file is batch size 1: each sample is encoded with only its own neighbours (one car at a time). Implemented as a block-diagonal mask on the neighbour SelfAttention (verified against literal batch-1 forward passes on 256 samples, max/mean abs difference in r of {'A': '0.091 / 0.0069 ft', 'B': '0.088 / 0.0058 ft'}, i.e. float32 kernel noise). The original code attends across all neighbours in a batch; see playground_data.json for batch-512 numbers.
meta.uncertainty: omitted: the decoders' predicted Gaussians are badly miscalibrated (see playground_data.json aggregate.*.sigma_calibration_20k).

headline.source: attacker retrained on batch-1 representations (attack_generic recipe, torch seed 72), evaluated on the attack_generic test split

headline.source: attacker retrained on batch-1 representations (attack_generic recipe, torch seed 72), evaluated on the attack_generic test split

grid.confusion_layout: [[true US-101 -> pred US-101, pred I-80], [true I-80 -> pred US-101, pred I-80]]

A_fl.source: W&B akibc123/battraj-federated-no-behavior/9gtyuhc3 ('Full 12 round run', created 2026-04-29T15:31:37Z); checkpoint battraj_fl_nb_*_best.tar (May 1) = round with min val_mse (round 9); this run's own final-round eval gave RMSE@5s 6.833 (polar metric)
A_fl.note: val_mse is in (ft, rad) polar units squared; rounds after pretrain_rounds use NLL training loss, hence the train-loss scale change

B_tappfl.note: TAPPFL encoder training has no trajectory decoder, so there is no RMSE/val-MSE here; utility proxy is the JSD (mutual-info) term. In-training adversary val_acc is unreliable: client-0 adversary collapses to the majority class (~0.543).

B_decoder_retrain.note: encoder frozen; rounds 1-6 MSE, 7-8 NLL. Model B uses the round-8 decoder (what produced the reported 7.28).

raw_input_probes.protocol: 120,000 random TestSet samples (rng seed 0), 80/20 split, MLP 256-256 (Adam 1e-3, 15 epochs), standardized features; no trained model involved. Ego history is the (r, phi) polar encoder input.

extra.other_lambda_note: No other TAPPFL-BATraj lambda point has both a measured attack accuracy and a measured trajectory RMSE. The Nov 11 fix variants (ctrl / uniform-target no-SN / +mean rep, lambda 0.5, 6 rounds) have only a linear-probe leakage (72.96 / 73.35 / 73.17 %) and no decoder/RMSE, so they are listed below for reference only.
